Description: Accounts receivable invoice to customer
Business Logic: Source of truth for recognized NET revenue (after trade deductions). total_amount reflects net revenue post-deductions. channel column enables direct revenue-by-channel analysis. customer_location_id → retail_locations. shipment_id links to fulfillment. Trade deductions are in trade_deductions table (ar_invoice_id FK), decomposing gross-to-net by program type.

Description: Line item on an AR invoice
Business Logic: Composite PK (invoice_id, line_number). This is where SKU-level revenue data lives — unit_price and line_amount ARE populated here. quantity_cases for volume, line_amount for revenue attribution by SKU.

Description: Receipt of payment against an AR invoice
Business Logic: Collection of AR invoices. amount is the payment received. This completes the order-to-cash cycle. Compare amount against ar_invoices.total_amount for collection rate analysis.

Description: Sales channel (retail, wholesale, e-commerce)
Business Logic: Sales channels (MASS_RETAIL, GROCERY, ECOMMERCE, etc.). channel_type column for B2B/B2C classification. Channels are the demand signal grouping for sales analysis. Each channel has trade programs (trade_programs.channel_id) defining deduction rates by type (scan, rebate, promo, slotting, off-invoice).

Description: Demand forecast for SKU at location
Business Logic: Forward-looking demand projections by SKU and location. forecast_version enables scenario comparison (e.g., baseline vs optimistic). location_type for polymorphic location resolution (same as inventory). forecast_type distinguishes baseline from promotional forecasts.

Description: Disposition action for returned goods
Business Logic: Records what happens to returned goods after inspection. disposition values include restock, destroy, rework, donate. No PK constraint in the database (composite key is logical). quantity_cases may differ from return_line quantity if partial disposition.

Description: Daily inventory snapshot by location and SKU
Business Logic: Point-in-time inventory snapshots. day column (integer 1-365) enables temporal trend analysis. location_type discriminates the polymorphic location_id: plant → plants, rdc → distribution_centers (type='rdc'), customer_dc → distribution_centers (type='customer_dc'), store → retail_locations. Store inventory is the majority of records by volume.

Description: Customer order header
Business Logic: Demand signal document. source_id is POLYMORPHIC: low IDs point to channels table, higher IDs point to retail_locations table. No discriminator column — resolved by ID range. retail_location_id is the non-polymorphic delivery destination. day column is the order date (integer 1-365).

Description: Line item on a customer order
Business Logic: Composite PK (order_id, line_number). Links orders to SKUs with quantity and unit_price. Revenue analysis can use either order_lines or ar_invoice_lines.

Description: Time-bound promotional event tied to a trade program and SKU
Business Logic: Promotional activities that drive incremental volume. Always linked to a promo_fund-type trade program. promo_type values: bogo, tpr (temp price reduction), display, feature. lift_pct is expected volume uplift as decimal (0.30 = 30%). incremental_spend is additional cost beyond the base promo_fund rate for this event.

Description: Retail store or customer delivery point
Business Logic: Retail endpoints representing stores across all channels. store_format (supermarket, convenience, warehouse, etc.) and channel columns enable segmentation. These are the final delivery points in the supply chain.

Description: Customer return (RMA) header
Business Logic: Reverse logistics entry point. source_id points to the retail_location where the return originated. dc_id points to the distribution_center where the return is processed (for inspection and disposition). return_date is day-integer.

Description: Line item on a customer return
Business Logic: Composite PK (return_id, line_number). Records returned SKU, quantity, and condition. condition column (sellable, damaged, expired, etc.) determines disposition path and recovery value.

Description: Outbound shipment to customer or distribution center
Business Logic: Fulfillment execution document. origin_id and destination_id are polymorphic WITHOUT explicit type columns. route_type encodes the compound pattern: plant_to_rdc, rdc_to_customer_dc, customer_dc_to_store, etc. Use route_type to infer origin/destination types. freight_cost for logistics cost analysis. IMPORTANT: Shipments come in 3-leg chains (plant_to_rdc → rdc_to_customer_dc → customer_dc_to_store). Only the last-mile leg (customer_dc_to_store) links to AR invoices. For cost-to-deliver / margin analysis, freight from ALL three legs must be allocated downstream to the end channel — upstream legs carry trunk-line and middle-mile freight that is invisible if you only follow AR invoice links.

Description: Line item on a shipment
Business Logic: Composite PK (shipment_id, line_number). Records what SKUs and quantities were shipped. quantity_cases for fulfillment volume, weight_kg for logistics weight calculations.

Description: Per-invoice-line deduction record linking trade program to AR invoice line
Business Logic: Transactional record of actual trade deductions applied per AR invoice line. Each invoice line gets N deductions (one per trade program for its channel). deduction_amount = list_price_per_case × quantity_cases × program rate_pct. For promo_fund deductions within a promo event window, promo_event_id links to the specific event. Key invariant: SUM(deductions per invoice) = gross_revenue - net_revenue exactly.

Description: Channel-level trade agreement defining a deduction type and base rate
Business Logic: Standing trade agreements by channel. program_type values: scan_allowance, volume_rebate, off_invoice, promo_fund, slotting. rate_pct is the deduction rate as a decimal fraction (e.g., 0.05 = 5%). Multiple programs per channel decompose the total trade discount. start_day/end_day define the agreement period.

Description: General ledger chart of accounts
Business Logic: GL accounts across 4 types: asset, liability, revenue, expense. account_code is the join key used by gl_journal (NOT id). account_name column (not 'name' — HasName mixin was removed from this class) provides the display label.

Description: General ledger journal entry
Business Logic: Financial backbone recording every financial event as double-entry journal entries. Balanced daily (debits = credits per day). reference_type + reference_id provide full traceability to source documents (purchase_order, goods_receipt, batch, order, shipment, etc.). is_reversal marks correction entries. Some GL postings are deliberate duplicates (reference_id suffix '-DUP'). A few days have small rounding imbalances.

Description: Price or quantity variance on AP invoice line
Business Logic: Records mismatches between AP invoice lines and PO terms. variance_type is 'price' (unit cost mismatch) or 'qty' (quantity mismatch). expected_value vs actual_value with variance_amount = actual - expected. resolution_status tracks audit progress.

Description: Accounts payable invoice from supplier
Business Logic: Source-side payables from suppliers. Links supplier_id + gr_id for three-way match (PO ↔ GR ↔ AP). total_amount for spend analysis. Some lines have price or quantity variances vs PO terms (recorded in invoice_variances table). Some duplicate invoices with -DUP suffix on invoice_number.

Description: Line item on an AP invoice
Business Logic: Composite PK (invoice_id, line_number). Records what was invoiced: ingredient, quantity, unit cost, line amount. These are the 'actual' values for three-way match against PO lines (expected) and GR lines (received).

Description: Payment against an AP invoice
Business Logic: Settlement of AP invoices. Some payments receive early-pay discount. net_amount = amount - discount_amount. This completes the procure-to-pay cycle.

Description: Goods receipt header confirming delivery of purchased materials
Business Logic: Inbound receiving confirmation. Links to an inbound shipment (shipment_id) and receiving plant (plant_id). GR confirms physical receipt of materials ordered via PO.

Description: Line item on a goods receipt
Business Logic: Composite PK (gr_id, line_number). Records actual quantity received per ingredient. quantity_kg is compared against PO line quantity for receipt verification and against AP invoice lines for three-way match.

Description: Raw material input to manufacturing formulas
Business Logic: Raw materials with real chemical/packaging names. Organized by category and subcategory (active_ingredient, base_material, packaging). bom_level=2 indicates raw material position in BOM hierarchy. cost_per_kg is the standard cost basis for cost rollup calculations through formulas.

Description: Purchase order header for procuring ingredients
Business Logic: Entry point of the procure-to-pay cycle. Each PO links a supplier to a receiving plant. order_date is day-integer (1-365). transaction_sequence_id provides causal ordering across all transaction documents. Lifecycle: PO → GoodsReceipt → APInvoice → APPayment.

Description: Line item on a purchase order
Business Logic: Composite PK (po_id, line_number). Each line orders a specific ingredient at a quantity and unit cost. These values are the 'expected' baseline for three-way match against goods receipt lines and AP invoice lines.

Description: Raw material and ingredient supplier
Business Logic: Suppliers with real company names. Some have -ALT suffix duplicates on supplier_code requiring entity resolution. country drives lead time and risk modeling. tier column for strategic segmentation.

Description: Supplier-ingredient catalog with cost and lead time
Business Logic: Sourcing matrix connecting suppliers to ingredients with commercial terms. lead_time_days driven by sourcing origin (LOCAL, REGIONAL, GLOBAL tiers). Multiple suppliers may offer the same ingredient at different cost/lead time/MOQ combinations. Basis for procurement optimization.

Description: Production batch output from a work order
Business Logic: Production execution record. product_type discriminates output: finished_good → SKU table, bulk_intermediate → BulkIntermediate table, premix → BulkIntermediate table (bom_level=2 sub-intermediates). bom_level mirrors formula hierarchy (0=finished, 1=intermediate, 2=premix). Mass balance: sum of input ingredient quantities (batch_ingredients) should approximate batch output quantity_kg / yield_percent.

Description: Actual ingredient consumption in a batch
Business Logic: Actual consumption records for production batches. quantity_kg records what was actually used. Expected quantity = formula_ingredients.quantity_kg × batches.quantity_kg. Useful for planned-vs-actual variance analysis and mass balance verification.

Description: Intermediate bulk product (e.g., paste, base compound)
Business Logic: Intermediate products in two tiers: primary bulks (bom_level=1) and premix sub-intermediates (bom_level=2). Bridges raw materials to finished goods in a variable-depth BOM (2-4 levels). Some bom_level=1 formulas consume premixes as ingredients, creating 3-level BOMs.

Description: Distribution center / warehouse
Business Logic: Distribution centers in two subtypes distinguished by type column: RDCs (type='rdc', regional consolidation hubs) and customer DCs (type='customer_dc', retailer/channel warehouses). Some customer DCs are multi-source (served by multiple upstream RDCs).

Description: Manufacturing formula (recipe/BOM) for producing a product
Business Logic: Manufacturing formulas at three BOM levels: SKU-level (bom_level=0), bulk-level (bom_level=1), premix-level (bom_level=2). product_id is polymorphic — bom_level=0 → skus table, bom_level=1/2 → bulk_intermediates table. Variable BOM depth (2-4 levels). Diamond dependencies exist (same raw material in both premix and parent bulk formula).

Description: Ingredient requirement within a formula
Business Logic: BOM line items with composite PK (formula_id, ingredient_id, sequence). quantity_kg is the per-unit requirement. IMPORTANT: ingredient_id is polymorphic — it can point to ingredients table (raw materials) or bulk_intermediates table (primary bulks or premix sub-intermediates). No discriminator column; must LEFT JOIN both tables to resolve.

Description: Manufacturing plant with production capacity
Business Logic: Manufacturing plants, each specializing in product categories. capacity_tons_per_day is the key constraint for production planning and scenario analysis. Plants are also origin/destination nodes in the transport network.

Description: Production line within a plant
Business Logic: Production lines within plants. line_type determines which product categories a line can produce. capacity_units_per_hour is the throughput rate. is_active filters operational lines (ontology has vg:sql_filter on the relationship).

Description: Transport route segment between two locations
Business Logic: This IS the transport network graph. Each row is a directed edge between two polymorphic locations. Origin types: supplier, plant, rdc, customer_dc. Destination types: plant, rdc, customer_dc, store. Network includes lateral RDC-to-RDC links for transshipment. Some DCs are multi-source (served by multiple upstream RDCs). Graph is not a strict tree — shortest-path and centrality analyses are non-trivial. distance_km and transit_time_hours are dual edge weights.

Description: Stock keeping unit - finished good for sale
Business Logic: Finished goods across categories (ORAL_CARE, PERSONAL_WASH, HOME_CARE). Some SKUs have -OLD suffix renamed codes with supersedes_sku_id linking to the replacement SKU. value_segment (premium/mid/value) drives margin analysis. price_per_case is list price; actual revenue is in AR invoices.

Description: Manufacturing work order for planned production
Business Logic: Production scheduling document linking a formula to a plant. planned_quantity_kg is the target output. Links formula (what to make) to plant (where to make it).
